title: Oracle Walk Run
statement: Let $d$ be a four-tape configuration on a Boolean input word, let $q$ be a dispatch state, let $p$ be an integer, let $m\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that at every integer $u<t$, the dispatch machine, when in state $q$ with the input symbol read from $d$ and with the work-tape heads at the positions determined by $p+mu$, prescribes no writes, moves the first two work-tape heads by $m$, leaves the other two stationary, and remains in state $q$. Then, for every $u\le t$, its configuration after $u$ steps from the configuration with those first two head positions set to $p$ is the configuration obtained by setting both positions to $p+mu$.
hypotheses_covered: Four-tape configuration $d$ on a Boolean input word
For each $u<t$, the stated transition action holds at the walk configuration
